response: We agree that numerical reproducibility and a MEMOTE score alone cannot establish predictive biological validity. The revision now tests biomass mass closure and precursor producibility, maintenance and uptake sensitivity, closed-boundary energy generation, loop-free exchange extrema, global GPR effects and transfer dependence. Original JGI inputs are recovered and all 477 model genes have sequence-supported public-locus mappings. The response below identifies the actual curation and the remaining biochemical evidence gaps; we do not present this draft as an experimentally validated strain-specific reference model.

The revision now makes three sequence-supported GPR edits: Bcd plus both Etf subunits, all six Rnf subunits, and inferred full-length PFOR homologs. The original model remains unchanged; the derivative has 483 genes and identical stoichiometry/bounds. Matched biomass, precursor/carrier, ATP and loopless checks, plus inclusion-minimal added-reaction sensitivity, accompany these edits. Unsupported complete pathway or measured-biomass claims remain excluded.

The phrase has been removed from the current manuscript. We describe a gapseq-derived draft reconstruction gapfilled using the stated anaerobic medium and simulated under explicitly defined nutrient constraints. The Methods also state that using the same medium for gapfilling and simulation makes baseline growth expected by construction.

C. sporogenes is retained only as a functional comparator for characterized reductive amino-acid gene-cluster architecture. It is not used as a close phylogenetic comparator. The Methods and Results now state this explicitly; the taxonomic analysis instead uses reciprocal ANI and accession-resolved Megasphaera references.

The 20%, 33%, 50%, 66% and 100% values are archived gutSMASH KnownClusterBlast fractions of reference-cluster genes with homologs, not pairwise amino-acid identities or query-alignment coverage. Table 2 uses one consistent term, candidate match, and gives the observed reference-gene fraction without treating a universal fraction as proof of an intact pathway. Separately, the new reviewed-reference DIAMOND candidate flag requires at least 30% identity and at least 70% coverage on both query and subject. All alignment values and provisional functional decisions are supplied in S54/S61. The archived gutSMASH invocation does not establish a separate custom per-hit coverage cutoff; none is invented.

The recovered gapseq output and pinned source resolve this point more precisely than the earlier response. At recorded commit c64db99b, both pathway and transporter searches default to 75% reference-query coverage and explicitly pass the filter to BLAST/DIAMOND. In the original files, all 20,283 reaction-table rows with recorded coverage and all 10,613 transporter rows have 75-100% coverage; none is below 75%. The Methods now report this evidence alongside the bit-score threshold of 200. Complete historical command-line recovery is not claimed. Reference-query coverage is distinguished from subject coverage and from gutSMASH cluster coverage.

The Discussion now explains why both calculations are needed. pFBA selects a representative minimum-total-flux state after optimizing biomass. It does not establish a unique secretion phenotype. FVA reports the feasible range of each selected exchange under a stated growth requirement; broad nitrogen/sulfur ranges and zero-butyrate states limit claims based on a single pFBA point. Selected loopless endpoints additionally test whether internal cycles explain those ranges.

The Methods define derivation_factor as the dimensionless multiplier in maxFlux = base_maxFlux * derivation_factor. It is a controlled perturbation of assumed model uptake capacity, not an empirical uptake measurement. The six-amino-acid multipliers derive from High-protein/EU-average AGORA ratios, whose dietary supply scale differs from the organism exchange-capacity scale.

Bcd/Rnf complex logic is corrected with sequence and neighborhood evidence, PFOR is annotated by full-length homology, and the numerical consequences for gene interventions and communities are tested. Remaining substrate specificity and target biomass measurements are explicit limits.

We agree with the central concern. The revised study no longer treats the archived high-butyrate reaction deletions as viable engineering designs or a feasible lactate exchange as evidence of necessary cross-feeding. Global GPR knockouts eliminate the attractive OK2-OK4 phenotypes, and donor-lactate-export blocking preserves the selected community growth states. The remaining conclusions concern constraint-dependent model behavior and robustness to explicit counterfactuals.

MJR8396C is now identified as a vaginal isolate at the start of the Abstract and Introduction and in the genome Methods. Gut-like media and the bifidobacterial partner are imposed model scenarios. We do not claim documented intestinal colonization, obesity association, fiber response or complex-carbohydrate degradation for this strain. The earlier inappropriate strain-specific citation argument is removed; related-strain physiology is identified explicitly as contextual evidence. The title describes a constraint-based analysis rather than an established gut ecological role.

Accession-matched sequence bytes were analyzed. Reciprocal skani/FastANI and both alignment fractions are supplied for DSM 20460, NM10, BL7 and closer reference genomes. skani ANI to the physiological comparators is 82.73-82.86%, with approximately 43-47% alignment fractions; it is not evidence of conspecificity. The exact assembly is assigned Megasphaera sp001546855 in GTDB R232, labelled as a release lookup rather than a newly run GTDB-Tk classification. Genome statistics are measured directly and plotted in Supplementary Figure S1: original JGI 2,426,262 bp/51.04337% GC and public assembly 2,453,897 bp/51.02898% canonical-base GC. The former comparative Figure 3 has been replaced by the current biomass/quality figure; the new sequence figure supplies the requested measurements without mixing assembly versions.

Bcd-Etf bifurcation stoichiometry was already present and remains balanced. Its erroneous ETF-only OR GPR is now corrected to require catalytic Bcd and both ETF components. Complete Rnf and inferred PFOR gene rules are also added. These annotation edits leave wild-type fluxes unchanged, so they do not erase the lactate benchmark mismatch. Uptake/maintenance/biomass and unsupported-reaction sensitivities retain that uncertainty; the lactate-centered biological conclusion is downgraded.

The original sensitivity and loop checks are extended with uniformly reconstructed exact-strain models, 432 new uptake/GAM/NGAM cases, 216 sequence-biomass/maintenance cases, ordinary FVA and 81 completed native fastSNP loopless FVA ranges. Template choice, gapfilling medium and nonunique reconstruction effects are explicit. Four AGORA formula-mass candidates, a common gross carbon budget and iME375 energy-cycle controls improve comparability. These are computational bounds, not experimentally calibrated growth rates.

An additional 1,920 native MICOM cases cover matched MJR8396C/NM10/BL7 models, sequence-curated sensitivities and original versus D-LDH-filtered 22L. Shared supplies are applied once per community biomass; taxon exchanges and growth are abundance weighted, with effective-supply monocultures and 4,320 exchange-FVA ranges. Removing unsupported 22L D-LDH eliminates D secretion without removing community growth. Direct comparisons retain four small growth benefits at 90% Megasphaera abundance with externally supplied lactate; all 116 feasible matched-growth monoculture butyrate intervals contain the community point. No-external-lactate and transfer-blocked controls do not establish lactate necessity. Equal selected member rates are attributed to regularization, not mutualism.

The full historical settings and bounded search remain documented. The same chemical target sets and native global GPR implementations were tested in all new exact-strain models. All eighteen tested OK2-OK4 minimal gene implementations in MJR8396C, NM10 and BL7 have zero growth, despite viable reaction-only counterfactuals. Nucleotide target-gene essentiality is independently retained after GPR curation. Growth-product envelopes and missing-target/GPR cases are supplied. The interventions are not promoted as viable engineering designs or independent convergent strategies.

The new matched panel tests all twenty amino acids and 190 pairs, including Leu/Ile/Val/Ala and Pro, with product fluxes alongside growth. No racemase is added solely to fit predictions: LarA-like matches and partial maturation evidence do not establish activity. Acrylate catalytic specificity, a complete Lar maturation system, Pdu/4-aminobutyrate route completeness and C5/C6 terminal chemistry remain qualified; no lack-of-gene claim follows from an absent model reaction.

Target measurements and unresolved polymer conventions still preclude a fully empirical absolute-growth ranking.

All 477 deposited genes now have sequence-supported public protein/locus mappings, and the annotation-only primary SBML adds NCBI protein cross-references and locus notes. Among assessable fully annotated internal reactions, the mass/charge audit detects zero imbalances; 195 MJR8396C and 147 partner internal reactions have incomplete/non-specific formulas and are reported separately. No unsupported proton-balance change was made.

The current revision tests rather than assumes the proposed lactate mechanism. Native community controls show that the selected growth states persist after donor lactate-export blocking, and global gene deletions overturn the attractive reaction-only engineering interpretation. We report conditional exchange in an imposed nutrient setting and do not present the simulations as verification of the organisms in coculture.

Core gutSMASH-associated chemistry already exists in the reconstruction; adding duplicate reactions would not curate it. We now correct the Bcd-Etf and six-subunit Rnf GPRs and add inferred PFOR associations using accession-resolved sequence and neighborhood evidence. Each edit is tested and separated from conservative bound sensitivities. Incomplete terminal or substrate-specific pathways are not invented from a cluster fraction; these remaining functional limits are explicit.

New models of the exact NM10 and BL7 assemblies, plus new MJR8396C and 22L controls, have completed a uniform gapseq pipeline and matched media, carbon, twenty-AA/190-pair, maintenance, intervention, FVA/loopless and native-community analyses. Both raw and sequence-curated/conservative community suites are supplied. NM10 potential Bcd frameshift evidence is traced to the public annotation and treated as uncertainty.

The analyses now share an explicit question about robustness of production and exchange predictions under comparable constraints. Historical nucleotide-associated gene designs are nonviable in all three new Megasphaera models; lactate transfer is not necessary in the tested community controls. Neither calculation establishes superiority of engineered monoculture or a stable mutualistic consortium. Experimental productivity, yield and stability would be required to compare applications.
